content.title: About
content.content: Pastry is a simple food made from a dough of flour and water that is deep‑fried. The frying creates a golden, crunchy crust while the interior stays soft and airy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flour‑and‑water dough is one of the oldest ways to prepare food.
Frying imparts a distinctive aroma prized in many culinary traditions.
In some cultures the basic fried pastry is served plain, while in others it is filled with various toppings.
Traditional frying uses high‑smoke‑point vegetable oils such as sunflower or canola.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Flour provides a quick source of energy through complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Unlike sweet baked goods, plain fried pastry contains virtually no added sugar.

items.title: Contains some protein
items.content: Flour supplies plant‑based protein that can contribute to daily needs.

items.title: Easy to prepare
items.content: Only a few ingredients and basic equipment are required.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds a significant amount of fat and calories.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing oil can generate trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat flour contains gluten, which may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease.

items.title: Burn hazards
items.content: Working with hot oil requires care to avoid burns.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pastries can be enjoyed as a snack on their own, served with sauces, sour cream, or vegetable purees. They are best eaten hot to retain their crisp crust.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pastries in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate and reheat in an oven to restore crispness.
